feature: About The 99 — the reference page, its gate and its figures
note: One route, and the close-out's job is the page a reader actually gets rather than the route existing. Seven rows, and they are ONE reader state rather than three. The page draws differently for a reader at version 0, one who is behind and one who is current, but the acknowledged version lives in `user_prefs` — no URL reaches those states, and `?next=` sets only the dismiss destination. The fixture account is in exactly one of them, so these rows differ in what they photograph (the head, the figures, the destination clause) and not in who is reading. The other two states are held by `about-page.test.tsx`, which renders `seen={0}`, `seen={ABOUT_VERSION}` and a version-2 page with one entry marked; a walk wanting the real thing would write the row and put it back, in the shape `probe:review` uses for its collection edits. The account menu row is deliberately NOT here. It is the page's permanent entry point and the one surface outside `/about` this feature changed, but every verb in this script reaches page content through `onPage`, which scopes to `<main>` — and the shell's account trigger sits outside it by construction. A row for it could only be written by defeating that scope, which is the rule that stopped two probes measuring the shell while naming a page. It is covered instead by `account-menu.test.tsx`, which asserts the row's position, its link, the roving wrap past it and its busy state, and by the close-out walk. No `shares` block: every figure mounts an app component in ONE place, so there is no second route to be the same as — the sameness question this feature has is whether a figure matches the surface it documents, which is what `figures.tsx` asserts per figure and what this sheet shows in a glance. A figure per row rather than one shot of 'the figures', each reached by NAME rather than by a pixel offset: the five specimens are spread across a page about nine screens long, so a single scrolled shot photographs one of them while its label names five — which is what the first version of this inventory did, and what the close-out table then repeated as though all five had been seen. The last row scrolls to the foot, because the destination clause and the dismiss are the only things down there and they are what `?next=` changes. The offsets came first and one of them overshot — the row labelled for the fit bar photographed the commander entries below it, which is the same overstatement in a different costume, so `scrollTo` was added to the shared script.
